question: Which of the following events of modern Indian history is NOT correctly matched?

options.text: Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon - 1905

solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandi March by Mahatma Gandhi – 1910**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the Salt March, was a major non-violent protest action in India led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It commenced on 12th March 1930 and concluded on 6th April 1930.
 
• The march was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly.
 
• Gandhi walked 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat to produce salt from seawater.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon - 1905**

 
 
• Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, ordered the partition of Bengal on 16 October 1905.
 
• This event led to widespread agitation and was a significant moment in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The partition was intended to divide the large province of Bengal into East Bengal and Assam, and West Bengal.
 
• It was later annulled in 1911 due to strong opposition.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement - 1942**
 
 
• The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Movement, was launched on 8 August 1942 by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It called for an end to British rule in India and was a significant event in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• The movement saw mass protests, strikes, and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• Despite the suppression by the British government, it united the Indian populace against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre at Amritsar – 1919**
 
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, Punjab.
 
• British troops under the command of General Dyer fired upon a peaceful gathering, killing hundreds of unarmed civilians.
 
• The massacre was a turning point in the Indian independence movement, leading to widespread outrage and condemnation.
 
• It highlighted the brutal nature of British colonial rule and galvanized Indian resistance.
